summary: Genetics researchers announced a five-year "Genographic Project," funded by the Waitt Family Foundation, IBM Corporation, and the National Geographic Society, to collect 100,000 DNA samples worldwide to map human migrations and relatedness. Details on data collection have not been specified, though the project may include fieldwork among indigenous groups and consumer kits, and it has been compared to the failed Human Genome Diversity Project; project leaders say they will make the information public and will not patent genes, but whether researchers using the data will be subject to licensing guidelines or able to patent discoveries remains unanswered. The announcement has drawn criticism referencing IBM's role in the Holocaust and National Geographic's alleged imperialist "gaze," and notes that previous genetic mapping projects focusing on ethnic groups have been controversial with allusions to early 20th-century racial anthropometry; participants emphasize studying "similarities" rather than "differences," but the project is expected to remain controversial.
